# srgn - a code surgeon

A `grep`-like tool which understands source code syntax and allows for manipulation in
addition to search.

Like `grep`, regular expressions are a core primitive. Unlike `grep`, additional
capabilities allow for **higher precision**, with **options for manipulation**. This
allows `srgn` to operate along dimensions regular expressions and IDE tooling (*Rename
all*, *Find all references*, ...) alone cannot, complementing them.

`srgn` is organized around *actions* to take (if any), acting only within precise,
optionally **language grammar-aware** *scopes*. In terms of existing tools, think of it
as a mix of `tr`, `sed`, `ripgrep` and `tree-sitter`, with a design goal of
*simplicity*: if you know regex and the basics of the language you are working with, you
are good to go.

## Supported Languages

- C
- C#
- Go
- HCL (Terraform)
- Python
- Rust
- TypeScript

## Quick Usage

The most simple `srgn` usage works similar to `tr`:

```bash
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn '[wW]orld' -- 'there'
Hello there!
```

Matches for the regular expression pattern (the *scope*) are replaced (the *action*) by
the second positional argument. Zero or more actions can be specified:

```bash
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn '[wW]orld'
Hello World!
$ echo 'Hello World!' | srgn --upper '[wW]orld' -- 'you'
Hello YOU!
```

### Language-Aware Scoping

`srgn` can scope to syntactical elements of source code. For example, searching only
within Python `class` definitions:

```bash
$ cat birds.py | srgn --python 'class' 'age'
11:    age: int
15:        self.age += 1
```

If standard input is not given, `srgn` finds relevant source files automatically and
processes them recursively at high speed.

### Actions

- **Replacement**: `srgn 'pattern' -- 'replacement'` — replace matches
- **Deletion** (`-d`): remove matched content
- **Squeezing** (`-s`): squeeze repeated matches into single occurrences
- **Uppercasing** (`--upper`): convert matches to uppercase
- **Lowercasing** (`--lower`): convert matches to lowercase
- **Titlecasing** (`--titlecase`): convert matches to title case
- **Normalization** (`--normalize`): Unicode NFD normalization (strip diacritics)
- **Symbols** (`--symbols`/`-S`): replace ASCII symbols with Unicode equivalents
- **German** (`--german`/`-g`): replace German alternative spellings (ae→ä, oe→ö, etc.)

Actions are composable. For example:

```bash
$ echo 'Koeffizienten != Bruecken...' | srgn -Sgu
KOEFFIZIENTEN ≠ BRÜCKEN...
```

### Scopes

- **Regex scope** (first positional argument): narrows processing to matches
- **Language scope** (`--python`, `--rust`, `--go`, `--typescript`, `--csharp`, `--c`, `--hcl`): scope to language constructs like `class`, `comments`, `strings`, `doc-strings`, `imports`, `function`, `struct`, `unsafe`, `attribute`, etc.
- **Literal scope** (`-l`): interpret the scope as a literal string instead of regex
- Multiple language scopes can be combined (AND logic by default, or OR with `-j`)

Dynamic queries use `~` to filter by name: `--go 'struct~[tT]est'` finds only structs
with names matching `[tT]est`.

Custom tree-sitter queries are supported via `--<lang>-query '<S-expression>'`.

### Working with Files

- Without stdin, `srgn` recursively discovers and processes files based on language
- Use `--files` to list which files would be processed
- Use `--files-with-matches` to show files containing matches
- Use `--inplace` to modify files in-place (use with caution)
- Use `--dry-run` to preview changes without applying them
- Use `--sorted` for deterministic output ordering

### Output Format

- In search mode (language scope, no actions): prints matching lines with line numbers
- In replacement mode: prints the full (modified) output
- Use `--only-matching` to print only matched portions
- Use `--line-numbers` to include line numbers
- Use `--count` to print only the count of matches

### Fail Conditions

Control exit codes based on match results:

- `--fail-any`: fail (exit 1) if any match is found
- `--fail-none`: fail (exit 1) if no match is found

### Installation

#### Prebuilt Binaries

Download a prebuilt binary from the
[releases](https://github.com/alexpovel/srgn/releases/latest).

#### Homebrew

```
brew install srgn
```

#### Nix

```
nix-shell -p srgn
```

#### Arch Linux

Available via the [AUR](https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=srgn).

#### MacPorts

```
sudo port install srgn
```

#### Shell Completions

Various shells are supported for shell completion scripts. For example, append
`eval "$(srgn --completions zsh)"` to `~/.zshrc` for completions in ZSH.

### Usage

```
srgn [OPTIONS] [SCOPE] [-- <REPLACEMENT>]
```

Run `srgn --help` for full usage information.

import os

    def run_cmd(self, args, text='', cwd=None):

        p = self.run_cmd(args, text)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, code, p.stderr.decode())
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout.decode(), output)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr.decode(), error)

    def test_replacements(self):
        self.check(['[wW]orld', '--', 'there'], 'Hello World!\n', 'Hello there!\n')
        self.check(['(a)(b)', '--', '${2}-$1-$$'], 'ab ab\n', 'b-a-$ b-a-$\n')
        self.check(['(?P<word>hello)', '--', '<$word>'], 'hello!', '<hello>!')

        self.check(['-L', r'\n', '--', ' '], 'a\nb\n', 'a b ')
        self.check(['(?<=a)b', '--', 'X'], 'ab cb', 'aX cb')
        self.check(['(?s).*?', '--', 'X'], 'unchanged\n', 'unchanged\n')

    def test_actions(self):
        self.check(['-u'], 'Straße café\n', 'STRAẞE CAFÉ\n')
        self.check(['-ul'], 'MiXeD\n', 'mixed\n')
        self.check(['-t'], 'the lord of the rings\n', 'The Lord of the Rings\n')
        self.check(['-n'], 'café naïve à\n', 'cafe naive a\n')
        self.check(['-S'], '<-> <-- --> --- -- != >= <= ...\n', '↔ ⟵ ⟶ — – ≠ ≥ ≤ ...\n')
        self.check(['-Si'], '→ ≠ –', '-> != --')
        self.check(['-g'], 'Koeffizienten Bruecken Strasse Busse\n', 'Koeffizienten Brücken Straße Buße\n')
        self.check(['-g', '--german-prefer-original'], 'Busse Masse\n', 'Busse Masse\n')
        self.check(['--german-naive'], 'ae oe ue ss AE OE UE SS', 'ä ö ü ß Ä Ö Ü ẞ')
        self.check(['-s', 'a|b'], 'aaabbbcccab\n', 'accca\n')
        self.check(['-d', '\\d+'], 'a12b3\n', 'ab\n')

    def test_unicode_regex(self):
        self.check(['\\w+', '-n'], 'cafe\u0301\n', 'cafe\n')
        self.check(['[a-z&&[^aeiou]]+', '--', '_'], 'hello world', '_e_o _o_')
        self.check(['\\p{Greek}+', '--', 'G'], 'hi αβγ', 'hi G')

    def test_machine_output(self):
        self.check(['--line-numbers', 'foo', '--', 'longer'], 'foo foo\nbar\n',
                   '(stdin):1:0-6;7-13:longer longer\n(stdin):2::bar\n')
        self.check(['--only-matching', '-u', 'foo'], 'foo\nnone\n', '(stdin):0-3:FOO\n')
        self.check(['--dry-run', 'foo', '--', 'bar'], 'foo\nnone\n',
                   '(stdin):1:0-3:foo\n(stdin):1:0-3:bar\n')
        self.check(['--line-numbers', '-u'], 'a\r\nb\r\n', '(stdin):1:0-1:A\r\n(stdin):2:0-1:B\r\n')
        self.check(['--python', 'comments', '--stdout-detection', 'force-tty'], 'x=1 # hi\n', '1:x=1 # hi\n')

    def test_python(self):
        text = 'x="outside"\nclass A:\n    "inside"\n    def f(self): return "yes"\n'
        self.check(['--python', 'class', '--python', 'strings', '-u'], text,
                   'x="outside"\nclass A:\n    "INSIDE"\n    def f(self): return "YES"\n')
        self.check(['--python', 'strings', '--python', 'class', '-u'], text, text)
        self.check(['--python', 'function-names', '--', 'new'], text, text.replace('def f(', 'def new('))
        self.check(['--python', 'strings', '-u'], 'x=f"hello {name} bye"\n', 'x=f"HELLO {name} BYE"\n')
        self.check(['--python-query', '((identifier) @x (#eq? @x "foo"))', '--', 'bar'],
                   'foo = foo + other\n', 'bar = bar + other\n')

    def test_other_languages(self):
        self.check(['--go', 'strings', '--', 'X'], 'package p\nimport "fmt"\nvar s="hi"\n',
                   'package p\nimport "fmt"\nvar s=X\n')
        self.check(['--rust', 'strings', '-u'], 'let s="hello\\nworld";\n', 'let s="HELLO\\nWORLD";\n')
        self.check(['--rust', 'fn~^test', '-u'], 'fn test_it() {}\nfn other() {}\n',
                   'FN TEST_IT() {}\nfn other() {}\n')
        self.check(['--c', 'strings', '--', 'X'], 'puts("hello");\n', 'puts(X);\n')
        self.check(['--typescript', 'strings', '-u'], 'let x=`hi ${name}!`;\n', 'let x=`HI ${name}!`;\n')
        self.check(['--csharp', 'strings', '-u'], 'string x=$"hi {name}!";\n', 'string x=$"HI {name}!";\n')
        self.check(['--hcl', 'variables', '-u'], 'variable "name" {}\nx=var.name\n',
                   'variable "NAME" {}\nx=var.NAME\n')

    def test_failures(self):
        self.check(['-u', 'x', '--fail-none'], 'none', '', 1, 'Error: Error applying: No input was in scope\n')
        self.check(['-u', 'x', '--fail-any'], 'x', '', 1, 'Error: Error applying: Some input was in scope\n')
        self.check(['(a)', '--', '$2'], 'a', '', 1,
                   "Error: Error applying: Error in an action: Action failed in replacement: Error in variable expressions: Undefined variable, unable to substitute: '2'\n")
        self.check(['--version'], '', 'srgn 0.14.1\n')
        p=self.run_cmd(['-d'])
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 2)
        self.assertIn(b'<SCOPE>', p.stderr)

    def test_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            root=Path(tmp)
            (root/'a.py').write_text('# foo\nx="foo"\n')
            (root/'b.py').write_text('x="foo"\n')
            p=self.run_cmd(['--stdin-detection','force-unreadable','--python','comments','--sorted','-u'],cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout),(0,b'a.py\n'))
            self.assertEqual((root/'a.py').read_text(),'# FOO\nx="foo"\n')
            self.assertEqual((root/'b.py').read_text(),'x="foo"\n')
            (root/'other.txt').write_text('# hello\n')
            p=self.run_cmd(['--stdin-detection','force-unreadable','-G','*.txt','--python','comments','--sorted'],cwd=tmp)
            self.assertEqual((p.returncode,p.stdout),(0,b'other.txt:1:0-7:# hello\n'))

if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()
